components.gap: Not every stopping/error guarantee of the selected source extent is shown to apply to the actual selection/stopping procedure. Wald p.130 (pdf p.14) asserts that (3.18)-(3.19) hold for the actual SPRT under dependent Gaussian autoregressive laws (x_1 and x_j - lambda_i x_{j-1} i.i.d. N(0,1), lambda_0 != lambda_1 in (0,1)); the treatment omits this instance, and thm:p15-se-dependent (parts 141-151; annex 79-90) keeps almost-sure termination as a bare hypothesis that is never established for that or any dependent process, so for the source's dependent procedure the guarantee is not shown to apply to the actual stopping rule; the '[p.~130]' pointer at line 150 stands in for the unsupplied example. Also absent: the source's strict sharpening alpha'+beta' < alpha+beta for the actual nominal-boundary test when a(alpha,beta)>A(alpha,beta) or b(alpha,beta)<B(alpha,beta) (p.133, pdf p.17); thm:p15-se-nominal (153-173; annex 92-107) states only <=.

components.gap: Not every approximation of the selected source extent is explained in relation to the actual selection/stopping procedure: (i) Wald's discretization route to arbitrarily fine approximations of gamma (p.136) and of EZ_n / E(n) (p.143) for nonlattice scores is not explained -- thm:p15-se-finite-recursion (parts 297-317; annex 242-248) covers only finite alphabets and the treatment is silent for continuous scores such as its own normal case; (ii) the source's sample-size argument that the nominal a(alpha,beta), b(alpha,beta) can only increase E_0(n), E_1(n) relative to the exact-error boundaries A(alpha,beta), B(alpha,beta), so that Table 1 understates the saving of the actual equal-strength procedure (pp.133, 146, 148), is absent from def:p15-se-normal-saving (360-386); (iii) the moment equations (4.47)-(4.50) obtained by differentiating the identity at t=0 and t=h under neglected excess, the use of (4.51) when B>0 with P(Z_n>=log A) near 1, and its mirror case B>0, A=infinity, Ez<0 (pp.149-151) are absent from def:p15-se-transform-approximation (411-463).

defect_observations.observation: Source p.130 (pdf p.14) Gaussian autoregressive dependent-observation example, and the claim that termination (3.11) holds for dependent observations under very general conditions, are not supplied; the treatment's dependent theorem only assumes termination and the [p.~130] citation points at an example the text never gives.
Source p.133 (pdf p.17) strict sharpening alpha'+beta'<alpha+beta when a(alpha,beta)>A(alpha,beta) or b(alpha,beta)<B(alpha,beta) is neither stated nor refuted.

Source discretization approximation for nonlattice scores (gamma at p.136, EZ_n at p.143) is not explained; the treatment handles only finite alphabets (annex 242-248) and gives no account for continuous score laws.

Source sample-size argument on nominal versus exact-error boundaries (pp.133, 146, 148: E_i(n) only increased by a(alpha,beta), b(alpha,beta); true saving greater than Table 1) is absent; Table 1 is represented by its alpha=beta=.05 entry only and the 'at least 47 per cent' range statement (p.148) is not reproduced or assessed.

Source moment equations (4.47)-(4.50) (pp.149-150), the mirror continuous-density case B>0, A=infinity, Ez<0 (p.150) and the use of (4.51) when B>0 with P(Z_n>=log A) near 1 (p.151) are absent; moments are mentioned only as 'derivatives at real tau=0'.

OC bounds rest on an assumed nonzero root h with phi(h)=1; no existence/uniqueness conditions are given for a general third law (source p.134 asserts existence under very mild restrictions, citing its reference [4]); the source facts h=1 under H_0, h=-1 under H_1 and 'gamma-bar minus gamma tends to zero as mean and variance of z vanish' (p.135) are not addressed.

Mirror halves of several proofs are delegated rather than written: 'analogous' (annex 11-12), 'follows similarly' (195-196), 'similarly' (259-261), 'the same calculation' (292-293, 343-344), 'by the same argument' (418-419), and the alternative-error half of truncation (437-439). Each is a sign/direction mirror of a written step; recorded under the audit rule, not used as the sole basis of any verdict.
